_doc: Chile, written by hand for the plans hour by hour (Manu, 2026-11-12). Patagonia (Torres del Paine, Puerto Natales, Punta Arenas) is in todo.json.

areas.season: Mediterranean: hot dry summers (December to February, above 30 °C), cool winters with smog that can hide the Andes. Spring and autumn are best.
areas.sleep: Lastarria or Providencia: on the metro, walkable, full of cafés.

items.name: Cerro San Cristóbal by funicular at sunset
items.best: Late afternoon, on a clear day
items.why: The whole city under the wall of the Andes, then dinner in Bellavista below.

items.name: Santiago on foot: the Plaza de Armas, the market, La Moneda, Santa Lucía
items.hours: A whole day at an easy pace
items.best: Tuesday to Sunday: most museums close on Mondays
items.why: The old centre in one loop: the cathedral square, a fish lunch at the Mercado Central, the presidential palace and a garden hill.

steps.what: Plaza de Armas and the Metropolitan Cathedral

steps.note: 1 h 30, one of the best in South America
seafood; the counters inside cost less than the big restaurants

steps.what: La Moneda palace and its square

items.name: A winery day in the Maipo or Casablanca valley
items.why: Carmenère in the Maipo under the Andes, or white wines in Casablanca on the way to the coast.

items.name: Cajón del Maipo and the mountains
items.why: A canyon into the Andes an hour from the city: hot springs, a hike, or El Yeso reservoir.

extras: After a rainy day the smog clears and the Andes show: go up a hill that day.
The Mercado Central's touts push the big restaurants; walk to the smaller counters inside.

areas.season: Mild all year by the sea; foggy mornings in summer. Rain in the winter months (June to August).
areas.sleep: On Cerro Alegre or Cerro Concepción, the walkable hills with the views.

items.name: Casablanca valley wineries on the way from Santiago
items.why: White wines grown in the sea fog, on the road to the coast.

items.name: The hills on foot: funiculars, street art, Neruda's house
items.best: Tuesday to Sunday: La Sebastiana closes on Mondays
items.why: A port city on 40 hills, linked by old funicular lifts and staircases covered in murals.

steps.what: Plaza Sotomayor; free walking tours start here (tip-based)
Up by the Ascensor Reina Victoria or Concepción
Murals and viewpoints of Cerro Alegre and Concepción
Lunch with a view over the bay
The lower town and the port by trolleybus

items.name: Viña del Mar and the coast
items.why: Beaches, gardens and the flower clock, 15 minutes by metro train along the sea.

extras: Keep the phone in the pocket in the port and the lower town.
New Year's Eve fireworks over the bay are among the biggest in South America.

areas.season: Desert at 2,400 m: hot, very dry days, cold nights; below −10 °C at El Tatio at dawn. Storms can close roads in January and February (the 'altiplanic winter').
areas.sleep: In San Pedro; all tours pick up there. Cash helps: few cash machines.

items.name: Stargazing in the desert
items.why: Some of the clearest skies on Earth, with telescopes and a guide.

items.name: Valle de la Luna at sunset
items.why: Salt-crusted ridges, a giant dune and the Licancabur volcano going pink.

items.name: El Tatio geysers at sunrise
items.why: Columns of steam over 80 geysers at 4,300 m, at their best as the sun comes up. A hot pool on site.
extras: Dress in layers you peel off: −10 °C at dawn, 25 °C by noon.
Swimwear under the clothes for the pool.

items.name: High lagoons and Piedras Rojas
items.why: Flamingos on the Salar de Atacama, two blue lakes under volcanoes at 4,100 m, and red rocks by a turquoise lagoon.

items.name: Floating in Cejar Lagoon, sunset at Tebinquiche
items.why: Float in water saltier than the sea, then a pink sunset on the salt flats.

items.name: Rainbow Valley and the Yerbas Buenas rock art
items.why: Hills of green, red and white minerals, and carvings of llamas and flamingos.

items.name: Pukará de Quitor
items.why: A stone fort of the Atacameño people on a hill above the oasis.

extras: San Pedro is at 2,400 m: do the 4,000 m trips (El Tatio, lagoons) after a day or two.
Lip balm, sunglasses and a hat: the air here is among the driest on Earth.
Park and community entrance fees are paid in cash pesos at each site.

areas.season: Rain in any month (temperate rainforest); December to March is mildest. The volcano shows best in the morning.
areas.sleep: Puerto Varas, on the lake facing the volcano.

items.name: Frutillar and its lake theatre
items.why: German settlers' houses, cakes (kuchen) and a concert hall on stilts in the lake.

items.name: Osorno volcano and the Petrohué falls
items.why: A perfect snow cone over the lake, emerald rapids on black lava and the lake of Todos los Santos.

steps.what: Drive around the lake to Ensenada
Lake Todos los Santos: short boat or the beach
Up the volcano road to the ski centre; chairlift if running

items.name: Chiloé in a day: Ancud, the penguins, Castro
items.why: Ferry to the island, penguins at Puñihuil (September to March), wooden churches and houses on stilts in Castro.

extras: A rain jacket every day here, even in summer.
The Cruce Andino crosses to Bariloche in a day by boats and buses over three lakes: a scenic way into Argentina.

areas.season: Wet and mild all year; the driest months are January and February.
areas.sleep: Castro, ideally in a palafito: a house on stilts over the water.

items.name: Castro: the stilt houses and the yellow church
items.why: Colourful houses on stilts and the wooden San Francisco church, one of the island's UNESCO churches.

items.name: Dalcahue market and the Achao church by ferry
items.why: A market of wool and smoked seafood, then a short ferry to Quinchao island and its oldest church.

steps.what: Curanto lunch: shellfish and meat cooked in an earth oven

items.name: Penguins at Puñihuil
items.why: Humboldt and Magellanic penguins on islets off the beach, by small boat.

items.name: Chiloé National Park at Cucao
items.why: Wild Pacific beaches and boardwalks through the rainforest.

extras: The ferry from Pargua takes about 30 minutes and runs often all day.

areas.season: Subtropical: 20–28 °C, short showers any time. The Tapati festival is in the first half of February.

items.name: Ahu Tahai at sunset
items.why: Moai against the setting sun, a walk from town.

items.name: Sunrise at Tongariki, the Rano Raraku quarry, Anakena beach
items.best: Leave Hanga Roa an hour before sunrise (sunrise is late here)
items.book: Park ticket and a certified local guide
items.why: Fifteen moai on one platform at dawn, the quarry where hundreds lie half carved, and a white beach with palms.

steps.note: the quarry is once per ticket

steps.what: Ahu Akahanga on the south coast

items.name: Rano Kau crater and Orongo
items.why: A crater lake and the village of the birdman cult on the cliff edge.

items.name: Ahu Akivi, the seven moai facing the sea
items.why: The only moai that look out to sea, and lava caves nearby.

extras: Inside the national park you must be with a certified local guide; the park ticket lasts 10 days.
Rano Raraku and Orongo can be entered only once each on the ticket: plan them on good days.
Everything is flown in: prices are high; bring pesos.
